cohort: The study included 27,382 women with singleton pregnancies who delivered at an Obstetrics and Gynecology clinic between 2001 and 2014.
finding: The study found a maternal GBS prevalence of 17.66%, with protocol compliance for prophylaxis not showing differences in NICU admission or perinatal death rates between treated and untreated GBS-positive pregnancies, and identified early gestational age as the only risk factor for chorioamnionitis.
gest_age: All singleton pregnancies carried to delivery were included; specific analyses were conducted for those between 34-37 weeks and >37 weeks, with early gestational age identified as a risk factor.
